correctness.rationale: For the explicitly labeled 14-vertex Fano-plane Levi graph, enumerated all independent four-sets (147) and independently reconstructed the robust-clique face set (3032 including empty; f-vector 14,91,364,854,1092,616). A newly implemented 14-stage element-toggle matching on the augmented face poset leaves exactly 92 critical five-faces, paired empty/vertex, and the entire 13846-arrow nonempty-face Hasse graph is acyclic by complete topological sort (3031/3031 faces). Thus its ordinary Morse CW model has one vertex and 92 five-cells and is wedge^92 S5 integrally. The total fourth cut complex is its combinatorial Alexander dual; integral duality shifts H5 to H6. The dual includes every face of size ≤3 and hence is simply connected, so integral homology Whitehead yields wedge^92 S6. Exactly 147 facets of size10 give pure dimension nine; nonzero H6 below top dimension obstructs pure shellability.
residual_risks: Finite exact Heawood case k=4; field Betti computation alone would not prove integral homotopy, but integral acyclic Morse model does.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is a canonical highly symmetric Fano incidence graph. Its exact fourth robust-clique and Alexander-dual total-cut homotopy types are natural missing parameters of a developing graph-complex theory, and the non-shellable pure nine-dimensional dual with lower-dimensional sphere homology gives a concrete structural counterexample. The paired integral computation distinguishes homotopy from mod-2 ranks and is not a numerical substitution from known k=3.
residual_risks: Result is graph- and robustness-specific; does not classify arbitrary incidence graphs.

limitations: Only k=4 Heawood (14 vertices), not general girth≥6 or other Fano-like graphs.
A nonindexed direct Heawood k=4 bounded-independence calculation could exist.
Earlier total-cut/robust-clique theorems beyond the inspected graph-family hypotheses might yield an unstated reduction.
